reference.description: upstream PR #1345 (merge f42daddf205f335fea6e200dad46049f33e71221): __eq__ and __hash__ use the cached arbitrary-precision numeric_range._len instead of len()

flawed-1.description: catches OverflowError in __eq__ (returns False) and __hash__ (hashes only start and step): wrong answers instead of a crash

flawed-2.description: fixes __eq__ only; __hash__ still raises OverflowError above sys.maxsize

flawed-3.description: above sys.maxsize compares (start, stop, step) tuples, so equal-content ranges with different stops compare unequal

flawed-4.description: changes __len__ to return min(self._len, sys.maxsize), breaking the len() OverflowError contract and making large unequal ranges look equal

alt-1.description: independent Claude Sonnet via `agent_runs alt` (runs/_alts/alt-1/more-itertools-1345/claude/trial-1/attempt-1, audit clean): reads the cached _len in __eq__/__hash__; converged on the upstream approach

alt-3.description: independent Claude Sonnet via `agent_runs alt` with a constraint forbidding _len and len() (runs/_alts/alt-3/more-itertools-1345/claude/trial-1/attempt-1, audit clean): STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT length source - a new _count() helper recomputes the item count from start/stop/step with divmod plus a _before_stop correction, instead of reusing the cached _len; the compare-length-then-ends logic of __eq__/__hash__ is unchanged
